questions.question: The modern-day ________ was molded by the renowned Tanjore Bandhu, consisting of the four Nattuvanars: Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnayya.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most traditional classical dance forms of India, originating in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, the ancient treatise on performing arts written by **Bharata**.
 
• The modern-day Bharatanatyam was shaped by the contributions of the **Tanjore Quartet** – Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam, and Chinnayya, who were collectively known as the **Tanjore Bandhu**.
 
• The Tanjore Quartet standardized the structure of Bharatanatyam performances and introduced the **margam format**, which consists of an organized sequence of items such as Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.
 
• Bharatanatyam is renowned for its focus on intricate **footwork**, graceful movements, and expressive **hand gestures** (mudras) that convey stories and emotions.
 
• It is often performed as a form of **devotional offering** to deities in temples, symbolizing the dancer’s union with the divine.
 
• Today, Bharatanatyam is celebrated globally as an iconic representation of Indian culture and classical art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam**__

 __
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form from **Kerala**, characterized by graceful, flowing movements.
 
• The name translates to "**Dance of the Enchantress**," and it is traditionally performed by women.
 
• Mohiniyattam integrates elements of both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, with a focus on **expressive storytelling**.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**__
 __
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama originating from **Kerala**.
 
• It is known for its elaborate **costumes**, intricate makeup, and dramatic storytelling based on **Hindu epics** such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• Kathakali is performed by male dancers, often depicting gods, demons, and other mythological characters.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**__
 
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form from **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It combines **dance**, **acting**, and **singing**, making it a unique performance art.
 
• Kuchipudi is often performed as a dance-drama, narrating stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• It is traditionally performed by both male and female dancers.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following options represents the correct flow of energy in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sunlight → Producers → Herbivores → Carnivores**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Energy flow in an ecosystem follows a unidirectional path starting with the **Sun**, the primary source of energy.
 
• **Producers**, such as plants and algae, capture sunlight through **photosynthesis** and convert it into chemical energy stored in organic compounds.
 
• **Herbivores** (primary consumers) feed on producers to derive their energy. Examples include deer, rabbits, and caterpillars.
 
• **Carnivores** (secondary and tertiary consumers) feed on herbivores or other carnivores to obtain energy. Examples include lions, wolves, and eagles.
 
• The flow of energy decreases as it moves up the trophic levels because of the **10% Law of Energy Transfer**, where only about 10% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level.
 
• This hierarchical energy flow ensures the maintenance of balance in an ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option: Sunlight → Herbivores → Carnivores → Producers**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because **herbivores and carnivores** depend on producers for energy, but producers do not depend on them.
 
• In ecosystems, producers are the starting point of energy flow, not herbivores or carnivores.
 
 
 
• **Option: Sunlight → Carnivores → Producers → Herbivores**__
 __
 
• Carnivores cannot directly utilize sunlight as energy; they depend on herbivores, which derive energy from producers.
 
• This sequence disrupts the natural order of energy flow in trophic levels.
 
 
 
• **Option: Sunlight → Herbivores → Producers → Carnivores**__
 
 
• This is incorrect because **herbivores** depend on producers for energy, not the other way around.
 
• Producers always occupy the first trophic level in energy flow.

questions.question: At 10 × 10⁴ Pa pressure and 300 K temperature, the volume of 0.09 mol CO₂ gas is 22.4 × 10−³ m³. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is decreased to 2 × 10⁴ Pa?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To calculate the **volume of a gas** under different pressure conditions, we use **Boyle's Law**.
 
• **Boyle's Law** states that, at constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. Mathematically, it is expressed as:

 **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**, where:
 
 
• **P₁** and **V₁** are the initial pressure and volume.
 
• **P₂** and **V₂** are the final pressure and volume.
 
 
 
• In this case:
 
 
• Initial pressure (**P₁**) = **10 × 10⁴ Pa**.
 
• Initial volume (**V₁**) = **22.4 × 10⁻³ m³**.
 
• Final pressure (**P₂**) = **2 × 10⁴ Pa**.
 
 
 
• Rearranging Boyle's Law to solve for **V₂**:

 **V₂ = (P₁ × V₁) / P₂**.
 
• Substituting the values:

 **V₂ = (10 × 10⁴ × 22.4 × 10⁻³) / (2 × 10⁴)**.

 **V₂ = 112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**.
 
• Hence, the final volume of the gas when the pressure is reduced to **2 × 10⁴ Pa** is **112.0 × 10⁻³ m³**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Concepts of Boyle's Law:**

 
 
• Boyle's Law is valid only if the **temperature** and the **amount of gas (number of moles)** remain constant.
 
• The law is widely used in understanding and calculating gas behaviors in **closed systems**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Boyle's Law:**
 
 
• Boyle's Law is applied in fields such as **pneumatics, scuba diving, and the design of syringes**.
 
• It is also used in the study of **breathing mechanisms** in humans and animals.

questions.question: Sawai Gandharva was associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kirana Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sawai Gandharva**, whose real name was **Rambhau Kundgolkar**, was a highly celebrated vocalist and teacher of the **Kirana Gharana**.
 
• The **Kirana Gharana** is one of the most prominent gharanas in Hindustani classical music, known for its emphasis on **perfect intonation (swara) and melodic elaboration (meend).**
 
• It is named after the town **Kairana** in Uttar Pradesh, India, where this style originated.
 
• **Sawai Gandharva** was a disciple of **Abdul Karim Khan**, the founder of the Kirana Gharana.
 
• He was instrumental in popularizing the gharana and trained several prominent musicians, including **Bhimsen Joshi**, **Gangubai Hangal**, and **Basavaraj Rajguru**.
 
• The Kirana Gharana focuses on the **slow development of ragas**, intricate ornamentation, and an emphasis on tonal quality.
 
• Sawai Gandharva's contributions to classical music were celebrated through the **Sawai Gandharva Festival**, an annual event held in Pune.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Benaras Gharana**__

 __
 
• The **Benaras Gharana** is associated more with **tabla and Kathak dance** rather than vocal music.
 
• It originated in **Varanasi (Benaras), Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It is known for its emphasis on **rhythmic patterns and intricate footwork** in dance performances.
 
• Prominent exponents of this gharana include **Ravi Shankar** (sitar).
 
 
 
• **Agra Gharana**__
 __
 
• The **Agra Gharana** is known for its emphasis on **voice production** and its robust and dynamic style of singing.
 
• It originated in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh**, and has a strong lineage of dhrupad and khayal singing.
 
• Artists associated with this gharana include **Faiyaz Khan** and **Ustad Vilayat Hussain Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Indore Gharana**__
 
 
• The **Indore Gharana** is primarily associated with the singing style of **Ustad Amir Khan**, who was known for his meditative and introspective approach to khayal singing.
 
• This gharana emphasizes the slow unfolding of ragas and uses a unique approach to **taans** and phrasing.
 
• It is relatively modern and blends elements from various gharanas.

__
 
• **Veereshalingam Pantulu** was a prominent social reformer in the **Madras Presidency**, which is present-day Andhra Pradesh.
 
• He is known for his efforts in promoting **widow remarriage** during the late 19th century.
 
• He established an organization to encourage and support **widow remarriage**, which was a revolutionary step in the highly conservative society of that era.
 
• He is considered one of the earliest reformers who worked against oppressive social practices such as **child marriage** and the stigmatization of widows.
 
• Veereshalingam Pantulu also started the first-ever **Telugu journal**, *Vivekavardhini*, to spread social awareness and reform ideas.
 
• He worked relentlessly to improve the status of women and was a pioneer in advocating for **education for women**.
 
• He is often referred to as the **Father of the Renaissance Movement in Telugu literature and society**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• He is best known for founding the **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company** in 1906 to challenge British monopoly in shipping.
 
• He was deeply involved in the **Swadeshi Movement** and worked towards promoting Indian industries.
 
 
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__
 __
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was a social reformer from Bengal who played a key role in advocating for **widow remarriage**.
 
• He was instrumental in the passage of the **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856**.
 
• He also worked for the **education of women** and the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **C Rajagopalachari**__
 
 
• **C Rajagopalachari**, popularly known as Rajaji, was an Indian politician, independence activist, and the last **Governor-General of India**.
 
• He was a key figure in the **Indian National Congress** and advocated for political and social reforms.
 
• While he contributed significantly to the freedom struggle, he was not directly involved in widow remarriage movements.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles entails "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment"?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 16**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16** of the **Constitution of India** ensures **equality of opportunity** in matters related to **public employment**.
 
• This article guarantees that no citizen shall face **discrimination** in public employment on grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.**
 
• The article further allows the state to make **special provisions** for the backward classes, Scheduled Castes (**SC**), and Scheduled Tribes (**ST**).
 
• It emphasizes the principle of **equality before the law** and ensures that every individual is given **equal access to government jobs**.
 
• **Equality of opportunity** under Article 16 is a cornerstone in ensuring **social justice** and inclusivity in the public sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 15**__

 __
 
• **Article 15** prohibits **discrimination** on grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.**
 
• It allows the state to make **special provisions for women, children, and socially or educationally backward classes.**
 
• This article is focused on promoting **social equality** and eradicating discrimination in society.
 
 
 
• **Article 17**__
 __
 
• **Article 17** abolishes **untouchability** and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• This article is aimed at ensuring **social justice** and removing historical injustices faced by **lower-caste communities.**
 
• It is one of the key provisions under the **Fundamental Rights** in the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 14**__
 
 
• **Article 14** ensures **equality before the law** and equal protection of the law to all individuals within the territory of India.
 
• It establishes that the state shall not deny to any person **equality** before the law or equal protection of the laws.
 
• This article forms the basis of the **rule of law** in India.

questions.question: The partition of ___________was annulled in 1911.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was announced by **Lord Curzon**, the then Viceroy of India, in **1905**.
 
• The partition divided Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam** with its capital at **Dacca (now Dhaka)**, and **West Bengal** with its capital at **Calcutta (now Kolkata)**.
 
• The stated purpose of the partition was to improve **administrative efficiency**, as Bengal was geographically large and difficult to govern.
 
• However, the partition was seen as an attempt to **divide Hindus and Muslims** and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal.
 
• It led to widespread protests, including the **Swadeshi Movement**, which promoted the boycott of British goods and the use of indigenous products.
 
• Due to the strong opposition and rising nationalist sentiment, the partition was **annulled in 1911** by the British government.
 
• Following the annulment, Bengal was reunited, and the capital of British India was shifted from **Calcutta to Delhi** in the same year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __

• It became a separate colony under British rule, and later gained independence in **1948**.

 __

• It was not related to the partition of Bengal, which occurred earlier.
 
 
 
• **United Provinces**__
 
 
• The **United Provinces**, now known as Uttar Pradesh, was a major administrative region in British India.
 
• It was not directly linked to the partition or annulment of Bengal but played a key role in the Indian freedom movement.

questions.question: What is the chemical name for the compound responsible for the cooling sensation in mint leaves?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Menthol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menthol** is an organic compound that is responsible for the **cooling sensation** experienced when consuming mint or mint-based products.
 
• It is a naturally occurring compound derived from **mint plants**, such as peppermint and spearmint.
 
• Menthol interacts with the **TRPM8 receptor**, which is a cold-sensitive receptor in the skin and mucous membranes, creating a cooling effect.
 
• It is widely used in various **applications**, including food, cosmetics, oral care products, and medicinal items like cough drops and topical analgesics.
 
• Menthol is also known for its **analgesic and soothing properties**, making it a common ingredient in balms and ointments for pain relief.
 
• The chemical formula of menthol is **C₁₀H₂₀O**, and it exists as a crystalline substance at room temperature.
 
• Menthol is utilized not only for its cooling effect but also for its **aromatic and flavoring properties** in products such as chewing gum, candies, and beverages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethanol**__

 __
 
• **Ethanol**, also known as alcohol, is a volatile, flammable, and colorless liquid widely used as a **solvent**, in alcoholic beverages, and as a **biofuel.**
 
• Its chemical formula is **C₂H₅OH**.
 
• Unlike menthol, ethanol does not produce a cooling sensation but may be used as a solvent in products containing menthol.
 
 
 
• **Caffeine**__
 __
 
• **Caffeine** is a natural stimulant found in coffee, tea, and chocolate.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.
The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.
At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappan burial practices** reflect the socio-cultural and religious beliefs of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The dead were generally laid in **rectangular or oval-shaped pits**, which were dug specifically for burial purposes.
 
• Burials could be classified into three main types: **primary burials** (where the body is buried intact), **secondary burials** (where only the bones are buried after the decomposition), and **fractional burials** (partial burial).
 
• Some burials were accompanied by **grave goods**, including pottery, tools, ornaments, and occasionally food items, suggesting a belief in life after death.
 
• Harappan burial sites such as **Kalibangan, Lothal, and Rakhigarhi** provide archaeological evidence of these practices.
 
• The orientation of the buried bodies varied, with some placed in a **north-south direction** and others in an **east-west direction.**
 
• Occasionally, communal graves were found, indicating the practice of **group burials.**
 
• These burial customs highlight the advanced cultural practices and spiritual beliefs of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.**__

 __
 
• The statement is incorrect because the **Harappan civilization** extended beyond Sindh and Punjab, spanning regions of **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and even parts of Maharashtra.**
 
• Important sites include **Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa (Pakistan), Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), and Rakhigarhi (Haryana).**
 
• This wide geographical spread reflects the vastness of the **Indus Valley Civilization.**
 
 
 
• **The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.**__
 __
 
• The statement is incorrect because the **Harappan script** remains undeciphered to date.
 
• The script consists of **pictographs and symbols**, with over 400 unique signs identified.
 
• It is believed to be written from **right to left** in some cases and **left to right** in others.
 
• The inability to decipher the script limits our understanding of the **language, administration, and beliefs** of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as granaries were found in multiple Harappan sites such as **Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, and Rakhigarhi.**
 
• Granaries were massive structures used for storing **grain**, showcasing the importance of agriculture in the Harappan economy.
 
• The granaries in Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro are particularly notable for their **engineering and layout.**
